title: Introduce transparent sidecar graceful-ejector and SLO-keeper for soft-path preservation
author: Riley Santos
release_notes: Hotfix: Add transparent sidecar ejector to remove misbehaving sidecars without full-region failover; SLO-keeper introduces a soft-path budget to prevent aggressive circuit tripping; telemetry: new ejection and soft-path metrics and dashboards.
description:
Motivation: A recent incident (SUP-2021) revealed that a misbehaving model-sidecar could amplify KV pressure and trigger region-level fallbacks. Existing circuit and load-shedding logic is conservative but reacts too late when a single noisy sidecar starts leaking latency/egress. This PR adds a lightweight transparent-sidecar graceful-ejector plus an SLO-keeper that preserves a soft-path budget to avoid aggressive region failover.

What this changes: 1) runtime: sidecar_health_detector module that observes per-sidecar ingress latency, outstanding-kv, and egress-saturation and marks a sidecar as candidate-for-eject when thresholds cross short windows; 2) graceful-ejector: a staged sequence that (a) drains new requests for the candidate sidecar, (b) migrates cached KV prefixes to peer nodes where applicable, (c) marks the sidecar as sidecar:ejected in the registry with an expiration and backoff; 3) SLO-keeper: a per-tenant soft-path budget that reserves a small portion of regional capacity for low-latency degraded responses rather than full failover; 4) telemetry: new metrics (sidecar_eject_attempts_total, sidecar_eject_success_total, slo_keeper_budget_used, slo_keeper_recoveries) and a small dashboard; 5) small fixes to fallback handshake so warm fallback respects in-flight KV leases.

Design notes: The ejector is conservative by default (v1 thresholds tuned to reduce false positives). The ejector is transparent: it does not change the client-facing routing decision set, only reduces load on the offending sidecar and signals the control plane. Ejection is timeboxed with exponential backoff and is reversible. The SLO-keeper implements a soft budget that decreases eviction aggressiveness instead of triggering immediate circuit-open.

Checklist: - [x] unit tests for sidecar_health_detector and ejector state machine - [x] integration test that simulates noisy sidecar and verifies traffic re-route and KV-preservation - [x] load test (bench) showing <2% extra token cost during ejection scenarios - [x] telemetry panels and alert (non-firing by default) - [x] docs: short note in runtime/CHANGELOG and SRE runbook update

Testing and rollout: CI: full unit + integration passed (See CI summary). Staged rollout: feature flag redwood.enable_graceful_ejector default=false; staged enable in canary region (us-west-2 canary pool) for 24 hours then wide. Monitoring: dashboards for sidecar_eject_* and slo_keeper_* added; initial alert threshold set high to collect signals. Rollback: flip feature flag to false; ejector reverses within two minutes for active ejections; emergency circuit: manual reclamation endpoint added to control-plane api to force-restore any ejected sidecar.

Risk and mitigation: False positives ejecting healthy sidecars is the main risk. Mitigations: conservative thresholds, multi-signature detection (latency + kv_pressure + egress), short ejection windows and exponential backoff, canary rollout. We also added an audit log entry for every ejection for post-incident analysis.

Related: SUP-2021 incident timeline, ENG-1983 proposal doc (linked in Linear).
